## Executive Summary

Recursive Language Model (RLM) architectures represent a paradigm shift from traditional single-pass Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). By decomposing complex, ambiguous inquiries into hierarchical execution trees, a supervisory **Prime Agent** coordinates specialized worker sub-agents that autonomously discover, interrogate, and verify evidence. 

Standard RAG architectures often suffer from context pollution and one-shot hallucination when dealing with multi-hop questions. In contrast, the Recursive Research Engine employs a closed-loop critique mechanism—cross-examining newly retrieved source passages against prior intermediate findings before authorizing report synthesis.

---

## Architectural Deep Dive

### 1. Hierarchical Prime Supervision
The Prime Agent functions as a meta-cognitive controller. Rather than issuing naive web queries directly, it analyzes topic topology and emits an initial DAG of 3–4 sub-inquiries. Each question is tagged with a strategic rationale and assigned an uncertainty boundary.

### 2. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Standardized Ingestion
Tool calls are decoupled from LLM vendor APIs by adhering to Anthropic's **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** standard. Search workers access external intelligence via standardized JSON-RPC `tools/call` schemas, supporting zero-credential web discovery (DuckDuckGo) and advanced semantic APIs (Tavily).

### 3. Closed-Loop Verification & Hallucination Auditing
The engine does not terminate on evidence retrieval. A dedicated **Verifier Agent** audits claims against raw scraped snippets:
$$\text{Hallucination Score} = 1.0 - \frac{\text{Supported Claims}}{\text{Total Claims}}$$
If the confidence metric fails to exceed the operational threshold ($0.75$), the verifier generates explicit gap descriptions and triggers a recursive planning cycle back to the Prime Supervisor.
